issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires the Farm to use a List<Animal> implemented with an ArrayList (initialize the ArrayList in the no-arg constructor). The provided solution, however, declares the animals attribute as a Queue<Animal> and initializes it with a LinkedList. This mismatches the specified attribute type/collection implementation and the getter/setter types, which can confuse students about which collection type to use and about the expected API (List vs Queue).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Farm implementation consistent with the problem statement: declare the animals attribute as List<Animal> and initialize it in the no-arg constructor with new ArrayList<>(); update the getter/setter and all usages to use List<Animal>. Alternatively, if using Queue/LinkedList is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to state that a Queue (LinkedList) is used instead of List/ArrayList.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly instructs the Farm to use a List implemented with an ArrayList for the animals collection, but the solution implementation declares animals as a Queue<Animal> and uses a LinkedList. This mismatches the concrete collection type named in the problem (ArrayList) and the expected abstraction (List) versus the solution's Queue/LinkedList types, which can confuse students mapping the requirement (ArrayList/List) to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution (and template) with the problem statement by declaring the animals attribute as List<Animal> and initializing it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-argument constructor. Alternatively, update the problem statement to allow a more general collection (e.g., Queue or LinkedList) and remove the explicit ArrayList wording so names/types are consistent across artifacts.
